title: Notification sends are delayed
briefing: Customer notifications are arriving late. Investigate before assuming either the delivery worker or provider is at fault.

actions.label: Inspect provider quota saturation
actions.criteria: Use when the provider rejects sends with a throttling response for a sender class.
actions.instructions: Compare provider quota counters and retry-after timing by sender class.

actions.label: Inspect provider credential errors
actions.criteria: Use when the provider response indicates credentials or sender authorization have failed.
actions.instructions: Compare credential version metadata against authorization response counts.

actions.label: Inspect the send queue
actions.criteria: Use when queue age rises and current evidence does not show external rejection.
actions.instructions: Compare queue age, claim rate, and active notification workers.

fallback: Capture one provider response code, the sender class, and the matching code table revision.

events.text: Customer notification delay rose above ten minutes. The alert does not specify a stage.
Send queue age is increasing and worker instances are active. Provider response outcomes have not populated.
The notification gateway emits sender-specific numeric status codes. For sender class B4, code 774 means sender quota exceeded. For class P9, 774 means credentials invalid.
The sampled rejected sends have sender class B4 and status 774.

debrief.summary: The provider throttled sender class B4. The same numeric status meant something different for another sender class, which made the mapping essential.
lessons: Decode provider codes in the context of their sender or account class.
Separate queue symptoms from the rejection that creates them.
